entries.title: DRAFT: Exact conditional single-site entropy bound
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED CAMPAIGN DRAFT; author proof saved, independent review pending. For real a, b>0 and lambda>0, let y(v)=b/[pi*((lambda*v-a)^2+b^2)] and Phi(t)=t*log(1+t). Then integral_R Phi(y(v)) dv=(2/lambda)*log((1+sqrt(1+1/(pi*b)))/2)<=log(1+1/(pi*b))/lambda. If V has an independent density bounded by R, E Phi(y(V))<=R*log(1+1/(pi*b))/lambda, conditionally on the cavity.
assumptions: For the conditional extension, V is independent of a,b and has Lebesgue density bounded by R.

entries.title: DRAFT: Conditional logarithmic cavity criterion for spectral purity
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED CAMPAIGN DRAFT; author proof saved, independent review pending. Let H_lambda=-A+lambda*V on l2(Z^3), with nearest-neighbor adjacency A, fixed lambda>0 and iid uniform V_x on [-1,1]. Delete site x; write Sigma_x(z)=<h_x,(H_lambda^(x)-z)^(-1)h_x> and b_x(E,eta)=eta+Im Sigma_x(E+i*eta). If J is bounded and open and sup_{0<eta<=1} E integral_J log(1+1/b_0(E,eta)) dE is finite, then almost surely the spectral restriction of H_lambda to J is purely absolutely continuous. This implication assumes the logarithmic bound and does not establish it.
assumptions: iid uniform site law; in particular own-site independence and bounded density

entries.title: DRAFT: Finite cavities cannot supply a uniform logarithmic bound
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED CAMPAIGN DRAFT; author proof saved, independent review pending. Let B be any finite-dimensional self-adjoint matrix, h a vector, J a nonempty bounded interval, and b(E,eta)=eta+Im<h,(B-E-i*eta)^(-1)h>. As eta->0, [integral_J log(1+1/b(E,eta)) dE]/log(1/eta)->|J|. The same limit holds with expectation for arbitrary random finite cavities. Thus the infinite-volume logarithmic criterion cannot be verified by taking eta->0 at a fixed finite volume.
assumptions: For the annealed extension the random matrix and vector are measurable and finite almost surely

entries.title: DRAFT: Bounded annealed density can coexist with atomic sample spectra
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED CAMPAIGN DRAFT; author proof saved, independent review pending. For the scalar random operator H=lambda*V with fixed lambda>0 and V uniform on [-1,1], every sample spectral measure is the atom delta_(lambda*V), but the expected spectral measure has bounded density 1/(2*lambda) on [-lambda,lambda]. The averaged Poisson-smoothed density has the same bound. Hence a bounded averaged density alone does not imply almost-sure absolutely continuous spectrum. This is an implication counterexample, not a counterexample to lattice delocalization.

entries.title: DRAFT: Cavity perturbation controls only positive regulators
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED CAMPAIGN DRAFT; author proof saved, independent review pending. For nearest-neighbor Anderson cavities on Z^3 with |V_x|<=M, |Sigma_lambda(E+i*eta)-Sigma_free(E+i*eta)|<=6*lambda*M/eta^2. If b_free(E,eta)>=b_*>0 on J and 0<eta<=1, then b_lambda>=b_*/2 whenever eta^2>=12*lambda*M/b_*. This gives integral_J log(1+1/b_lambda)<=|J|*log(1+2/b_*) only above that cutoff; it supplies no fixed-positive-lambda eta->0 bound.
assumptions: For the lower-bound consequence assume the displayed uniform free-cavity lower bound

entries.title: DRAFT: Small bounded disorder preserves some window mass
entries.statement: UNREVIEWED CAMPAIGN DRAFT; author proof saved, independent review pending. Let H_0=-A be nearest-neighbor hopping on l2(Z^3), and J any nonempty open interval contained in (-6,6). For any M<infinity, there is lambda_J,M>0 such that for every diagonal potential with |V_x|<=M and 0<lambda<lambda_J,M, the spectral projection of H_0+lambda*V onto J is nonzero. This follows from norm continuity of continuous functional calculus and positive free spectral weight, and says nothing about purity.
assumptions: J nonempty open subinterval of the free band
lambda sufficiently small depending on J,M

entries.title: UNPROVED: infinite-volume logarithmic cavity bound
entries.statement: For the infinite-volume nearest-neighbor Anderson operator on Z^3 with iid uniform potentials in [-1,1], there exist a fixed nonempty bounded open J inside (-6,6) and lambda_0>0 such that for every fixed 0<lambda<lambda_0, sup_{0<eta<=1} E integral_J log(1+1/[eta+Im<h_0,(H_lambda^(0)-E-i*eta)^(-1)h_0>]) dE is finite. This is an unproved input, not a theorem or a solved-parent claim. The associated conditional reduction does not address GOE statistics.

relations.rationale: The conditional reduction first converts logarithmic cavity control into the single-site Phi entropy bound by the exact L1 identity.
The L2 conclusion explicitly assumes LG, which is separately labeled unproved.
L3 concerns finite matrices and warns against replacing the explicitly infinite-volume LG input by a fixed finite cavity.
C1 refutes a weaker first-moment-only implication, while L2 adds a uniform entropy hypothesis.
The deterministic L4 comparison reaches only positive regulator cutoffs and leaves the all-eta LG bound open.
L5 supplies nonzero mass for small bounded disorder; L2 supplies purity only conditional on LG.
